text:
alyssa: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection perf change on canary we see a steady KV cache RSS drift on long contexts. Not a single crash, but fragmentation + paging causing 15-30% latency tail spikes.
jonah: Seen similar in my load tests this morning. RSS climbs ~6GB over 12h on synth long-context workload.
maria: any flamegraphs or perf reports?
alyssa: yes — attached snippet from perf top and a small sampling of /proc/<pid>/smaps. main signal is many small anonymous mmaps ~4k/8k left as 'holes' that never get reused. perf shows ~10% time in page reclaim under load.
alyssa: quick paste: ```
# perf top sample:
  samples  10.4%  server.bin  [.] slab_allocator::alloc_small
  samples   9.1%  server.bin  [.] kv_cache::insert
  samples   4.8%  libpthread.so [.] futex_wait
```
alyssa: and smaps snippet: ```
AnonHugePages:        0 kB
Rss:             16384000 kB
Private_Dirty:    204800 kB
Size:            18000000 kB
Referenced:      15000000 kB
"""
jonah: interesting — looks like allocator churn producing many tiny allocations that can't be coalesced because we've pinned alignment to 4KB and don't aggressively munmap.
maria: is this after the kernel change to prefer fastvec/avx kernels? could be different codepaths producing different allocation size mix.
alyssa: yes, changed kernel selection heuristics two weeks ago; the new runtime path uses batched kv writes and a new slab suballocator for short-lived contexts. That suballocator avoids munmap to be fast, but seems to keep many partially-used slabs.
rachel: can we reproduce locally with a synthetic long-context generator?
alyssa: repro command: ```
REDWOOD_KV_ALLOC_DEBUG=1 ./bin/server --kv-warmup 200k --long-context 64k --test-duration 2h
# then run: ./tools/kv-frag-analyzer --pid $PID --hist 10m
```
jonah: I'll run that on a c6 test node tonight and attach kv-frag-analyzer output. Expect to see high "free-slot-count" on odd block sizes.
maria: initial theory: allocator blocksize buckets omitted mid-range sizes (2KB-6KB) so long contexts create many 5KB-ish entries that fall into 8KB bucket leaving 3KB wasted each. Over many entries that adds up.
alyssa: proposal sketches: 1) add 'age tag' per slab page and opportunistic scavenge when age > X and free ratio > Y; 2) introduce a mid-range 6KB bucket and test memory/latency tradeoff; 3) background compaction thread that consolidates partially-filled slabs every N minutes (no stop-the-world).
achel: typo — rachel: background compaction must be IO/cpu-limited; prefer rate-limited work with backoff.
jonah: counters and telemetry we need: per-bucket free/fill, average lifetime by bucket, number of munmap events, page fault rate, and page reclaim stalls.
maria: also test with glibc's MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_  and jev_malloc tuning — maybe allocator interacts badly with kernel vm heuristics.
alyssa: perf-bot: run microbench (10min) of new 6KB bucket and age-scavenge sim on c6-small and report mem/delta.
perf-bot: queued: microbench-v2 on c6-small. estimated 12m. results will post in thread when done.
jonah: actionable: I'll run repro and frag-analyzer tonight, collect smaps and perf. Maria can prototype 6KB bucket locally? Alyssa will draft scavenge proto.
maria: yes, can prototype quickly — I can also simulate workload in tools/kv-loadgen to see fill/evict distribution.
alyssa: thanks. If noisy tail persists after scavenge prototype we should consider a compact-on-evict policy: when free-ratio > 0.35 trigger targeted compaction for top-N hottest slabs.
rachel: agree but we should gate compaction behind telemetry to avoid thrashing. Also add e2e test with long-context 48h run for Dedicated plan to ensure no silent growth.
alyssa: noted. I'll open a RFC with benchmark numbers and a minimal patch for age-tagging. tl;dr: root cause looks like suballocator design + kernel-selection change altering allocation-size mix. Fix path: tune mid-size buckets + age-based scavenging + telemetry.
jonah: perfect. assign follow-ups in RFC and /eng-runtime sprint. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — will post early prototype by EOD tomorrow.
